newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil army dispatched to control rioting police.
newsitem.headline: Brazil army dispatched to control rioting police.

text.p: Brazilian army troops were dispatched on Tuesday to the capitol building in Minas Gerais state to control hundreds of policemen rioting in a dispute over wages, a presidential spokesman said.

Gov. Eduardo Azeredo requested the help of federal troops when hundreds of military police attempted to storm the capitol building in Belo Horizonte after five hours of peaceful protest, the spokesman said.
Shots were exchanged between the protesters and another group of military police who were guarding the capitol. One policeman was shot in the head and was reported in stable condition.
The spokesman said that calm had been restored by Tuesday evening and that police would meet with state officials on Wednesday to discuss a salary hike.
Vice President Marco Marciel authorised the use of up to 900 federal troops in the operation, the presidential spokesman said. It was unclear how many were actually sent to the capitol building.
